page.home.s: Your PC at a glance. Everything here is safe and can be undone.
page.clean.s: Removes files that are no longer used. Tick what you want and press Scan to see the sizes first.
page.tweaks.s: Settings that make Windows faster and nicer. Each one can be switched off again at any time.
page.repair.s: Fix Windows Update, system files and create restore points.
page.tools.s: Network, updates, startup apps, security and more.
page.settings.s: Language, theme, automation and information about the app.
restart.banner: ⟳ Restart needed to apply some changes
home.tip: Tip: start with Windows settings › "Apply all recommended", then run a Quick cleanup. Everything can be undone.
clean.age.d: Files that changed recently are kept, because a program may still need them (e.g. an unfinished installation).
clean.note.winold: Windows did not remove everything. Try again after a restart.
cat.usertemp.d: Leftovers from programs and installers in your temp folder.
cat.wintemp.d: Leftovers from Windows itself and from installations.
cat.wucache.d: Update files that are already installed. Windows downloads them again if needed.
cat.doptim.d: Update pieces that Windows keeps to share with other PCs.
cat.inetcache.d: Cache used by Windows components and old Internet Explorer.
cat.dumps.d: Memory files created after a crash or blue screen. Often hundreds of MB.
cat.logs.d: Windows CBS/DISM logs older than 14 days.
cat.browsers.d: Chrome, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi and Firefox cache. Passwords, history and cookies are NOT touched.
cat.browsers.w: Close the browsers first; open ones are skipped. Pages load a little slower the first time.
cat.shader.d: NVIDIA/AMD/DirectX shader cache. Fixes graphics glitches after a driver update.
cat.shader.w: Games may stutter a little the first time, until the cache is rebuilt.
cat.recycle.d: Empties the Recycle Bin on all drives.
cat.recycle.w: PERMANENT deletion: files in the bin cannot be recovered.
cat.winold.d: Left behind after a big Windows upgrade. Often 20+ GB.
cat.winold.w: After this you can no longer go back to the previous Windows version.
cat.component.d: Removes old versions of system files left by updates.
cat.component.w: Takes a few minutes. Installed updates can no longer be uninstalled.
cat.dns.d: Clears saved website addresses. Helps when a site does not open. The VPN keeps working.
tw.rec.none: All recommended settings were already on.
tw.restore.confirm: Restore every setting on this page exactly as it was before you changed it here?
tw.restore.done: All settings were restored. Restart to apply them fully.
tw.restore.none: You have not changed any setting from here, so there is nothing to restore.
tw.visualfx.w: Turns off window and taskbar animations, shadows and "peek". Keeps thumbnails and smooth fonts. Makes older or weaker PCs feel faster.
tw.visualfx.a: Only how things look. Fully applied after sign-out or restart.
tw.transparency.l: No transparency in menus and taskbar
tw.transparency.w: Turns off the "frosted glass" effect in Start, taskbar and windows. Lightens the load on the graphics card, mostly on laptops.
tw.transparency.a: Only how things look. Applies immediately.
tw.fileext.w: Shows the ending of every file name, so you can instantly spot a fake "movie.mp4.exe". Very useful for safety, especially with downloaded files.
tw.fileext.a: Only how names appear in File Explorer. Applies immediately (or press F5).
tw.menudelay.w: Menus and sub-menus open almost instantly (100 ms instead of 400 ms).
tw.menudelay.a: Only menu speed. Applies after sign-out or restart.
tw.nostoreopen.l: No Microsoft Store for unknown files
tw.nostoreopen.w: When you open an unknown file type, Windows shows your own programs instead of sending you to the Store.
tw.copymove.l: "Copy to..." and "Move to..." in the right-click menu
tw.copymove.w: Adds two options to send files to another folder without copy and paste.
tw.copymove.a: On Windows 11 they appear under "Show more options" (or directly with the classic right-click).
tw.classicmenu.w: Right-click shows all options directly (7-Zip, Notepad++, VS Code...) without "Show more options".
tw.classicmenu.a: Only the right-click menu. Needs a File Explorer restart (button at the top).
tw.thispc.w: Instead of Home (recent files, OneDrive), File Explorer opens directly on your drives.
tw.thispc.a: Only where File Explorer opens. Applies to the next window.
tw.endtask.w: Right-click a program on the taskbar to close it when it freezes, without Task Manager.
tw.hags.w: The graphics card manages its own memory. Lowers latency in games and is required for NVIDIA DLSS Frame Generation.
tw.hags.a: Needs a restart and a fairly new graphics card (NVIDIA GTX 1000+, AMD RX 5000+, Intel Arc). If you notice stutter, turn it off.
tw.windowed.w: A Windows 11 setting that lowers input lag and improves frame pacing in windowed and borderless games.
tw.windowed.a: DirectX 10/11 games only. Applies the next time the game starts.
tw.gamemode.w: While you play, Windows gives priority to the game and postpones updates and notifications. Usually already on.
tw.gamedvr.w: Stops Xbox Game Bar background recording, which can lower FPS.
tw.gamedvr.a: You cannot record clips with Win+Alt+G.
tw.mouse.w: Turns off "Enhance pointer precision". The pointer always moves the same distance for the same hand movement, which helps aiming in games.
tw.mouse.a: The mouse feels a little different at first. Applies immediately.
tw.startupdelay.w: Removes the few seconds Windows waits before starting startup programs.
tw.startupdelay.a: On a hard disk (HDD) the first seconds may feel heavier. On an SSD, only benefit.
tw.bgapps.l: No Store apps in the background
tw.bgapps.w: Microsoft Store apps (Weather, Phone Link...) do not run when closed. Saves memory and battery.
tw.bgapps.a: Store apps will not notify you while closed. Normal programs (Chrome, Discord, Mullvad) are not affected.
tw.widgets.w: Disables the Widgets board, which runs constantly in the background and uses a lot of RAM.
tw.widgets.a: You lose the news/weather board (Win+W). Applies after a restart.
tw.ads.w: Stops suggested apps in Start, tips, automatic installation of promoted apps and the advertising ID.
tw.delivopt.l: No update sharing with other PCs
tw.delivopt.w: By default Windows uploads pieces of updates to other PCs (like a torrent). This keeps your upload bandwidth for you.
tw.delivopt.a: Updates still download normally from Microsoft.
hvci.d: Protects the core of Windows from malware. In some games it can lower FPS slightly (usually 0-5%). Microsoft says gamers may turn it off while playing. Because it is a security setting, this app does not change it for you.
rep.wu.d: For update errors such as 0x80070490 or 0x80070002. Stops the update services, renames the SoftwareDistribution and catroot2 folders so Windows recreates them clean, and starts the services again.
rep.wu.a: Update history in Settings will look empty. Old folders are kept as a backup for 14 days.
rep.wu.confirm: Repair Windows Update now? It takes about a minute.
rep.wu.after: Done! Restart the PC and then try "Check for updates" again.
rep.sys.d: Checks and repairs damaged Windows files. Helps with crashes, strange errors and failed updates.
rep.sys.a: Takes 10-30 minutes and keeps the PC busy. Your files are not touched.
rep.sys.confirm: Start the system repair? It takes 10-30 minutes.
rep.sys.toast: System repair finished. See the results in John's Toolkit.
rep.rp.d: Saves a snapshot of system settings so you can go back if something goes wrong.
rep.rp.a: Uses a little disk space. Windows allows one per 24 hours.
rep.rp.open: Go back to a restore point
rep.ts.d: Microsoft's own tools for Windows Update, network, sound and more.
rep.dism.ok: DISM: the Windows image is healthy.
rp.exists: No new restore point: Windows allows one per 24 hours, so a recent one already exists.
wu.renamefail: Could not rename {0} (in use). Restart and try again.
tools.intro.d: Network & VPN, leftovers, the health report and large files still open in the classic console window (Greek only). They will move into this window in the next version.
tools.net.d: Active connections, programs outside the VPN, known malicious IPs, live monitoring.
tools.upd.d: Choose which programs to update, with warnings for risky ones and frozen programs.
tools.startup.d: Turn programs that start with Windows on or off.
tools.leftovers.d: Broken shortcuts, ghost entries and orphaned tasks, with backup and restore.
tools.security.d: Antivirus, firewall, UAC, remote desktop, SMBv1, Secure Boot and a quick virus scan.
tools.health.d: Disk health and temperature, memory and battery report.
tools.bigfiles.d: Shows what takes up space on your disk.
set.auto.d: Every Sunday at 20:00 cleans unused temporary files, update downloads, error reports and DNS in the background. Safe with VPN and downloads.
set.auto.fail: Could not change the weekly cleanup.
set.shortcut.ok: A shortcut was added to your desktop.
set.update.fail: Could not check for updates. Check your internet connection.
set.update.new: Version {0} is available. Open the download page?
about.d:
Version {0} · by nmx88 · for Windows 10 and 11
Free and open source (MIT license). Use at your own risk: every change can be undone, but keep backups of important files.
Web services used only when you ask: ip-api.com (non-commercial use), abuse.ch, Emerging Threats, Mullvad, VirusTotal (search only).
task.busy: Another task is running. Please wait for it to finish.
task.closebusy: A task is still running. Close anyway?
code.0xFFFFFFFF: The Windows tool could not be started (maybe blocked by antivirus or missing).
code.0x800F0806: Windows is waiting for a restart to finish an update. Restart and run it again.
code.0x800F081F: Repair files were not found. Usually fixed by Windows Update and trying again.
code.0x800F0906: Repair files could not be downloaded. Check the internet connection.
code.0x80070070: There is not enough free disk space.
code.0x800705B4: The task took too long and stopped. Try again.
code.0x80070005: Access denied (maybe blocked by another program, e.g. antivirus).
code.0x80073D02: The program was open. Close it and try again.
code.0x00000BC2: Finished, but a restart is required.
code.0x00000652: Another installation is running. Wait for it and try again.
code.0x00000643: The installer failed (a general error of the program itself).
spec.title: Your PC
spec.copied: PC specs copied to the clipboard.
tools.cardhint: Click to open in classic mode
page.apps.s: Startup programs, program updates and pre-installed apps.
page.security.s: A quick check of your PC's protection. Nothing is changed without your click.
st.intro: Programs that open by themselves when Windows starts. Fewer startup apps = Windows ready sooner. Switching one off does not uninstall it; you can still open it normally.
st.hint.vpn: VPN: keep it on, so the VPN starts before anything else.
st.hint.security: Windows Security icon: keep it on.
st.hint.torrent: Torrent: make sure your VPN has a kill switch (e.g. Mullvad Lockdown mode) if this starts automatically.
upd.intro: Finds newer versions of your programs (winget). Safe updates are ticked; risky ones are explained and left unticked. "Freeze" hides a program from future updates.
upd.nowinget: winget was not found. Install or update "App Installer" from the Microsoft Store.
upd.none: ✓ All your programs are up to date!
upd.r.major: Big version change ({0} → {1}). Usually fine, but the look or settings may change.
upd.r.vpn: The VPN disconnects briefly during the update. Pause your downloads first.
upd.r.torrent: The torrent program closes to update.
upd.r.docker: Stops all containers and may ask to update WSL.
upd.r.vbox: Close your virtual machines first. Network drivers are reinstalled (internet drops for a moment).
upd.r.tailscale: The Tailscale connection drops for a moment.
upd.r.postgres: Restarts the database. Close anything that uses it.
upd.r.vs: Huge, and often gets stuck through winget. Update it from the Visual Studio Installer.
upd.r.adobe: Updates better from inside the program; often fails through winget.
upd.r.self: Updates itself when you open it.
upd.r.skip: Not needed for everyday use. You can freeze it.
upd.freeze.d: Hide this program from future updates
upd.pinned.d: Not shown in updates until you unfreeze it.
upd.pinfail: Could not change it. Update "App Installer" from the Store.
upd.confirm: Update {0} programs now? They may close while updating.
upd.vpnwarn: ⚠ Your VPN is in the list: it will disconnect for a moment. Pause your downloads first.
bl.intro: Microsoft apps that came with Windows. Tick the ones you do not use. You can reinstall any of them for free from the Microsoft Store.
bl.none: ✓ None of the known unneeded apps are installed.
bl.n.phone: connects your phone to the PC
sec.scan.confirm: Run a quick virus scan with Microsoft Defender? It takes a few minutes.
sec.scan.done: The quick virus scan finished. If anything was found, Windows Security will notify you.
sec.scan.nodef: Microsoft Defender was not found (another antivirus may be in use).
sec.av.def: Microsoft Defender: real-time protection is on
sec.av.sig: Virus definitions are {0} days old: run Windows Update
sec.av.none: NO active virus protection was found!
sec.rdp.on: Remote Desktop is on: turn it off if you do not use it
sec.smb1.on: The old SMBv1 protocol is on (targeted by old malware)
sec.tpm.none: No TPM found (or it is turned off in BIOS)
sec.upd.old: Last Windows update: {0} days ago. Run Windows Update
sec.hvci.off: Memory integrity: off (optional, see Windows settings › Security)
sec.ext.shown: File extensions are visible (fake .exe files are easy to spot)
sec.ext.hidden: File extensions are hidden: a fake "video.mp4.exe" looks like a video
sec.remote: Remote access programs installed: {0}. Keep them only if you use them.
pw.d: How hard the processor works. Higher performance = faster response, more power use and heat.
pw.fail: This plan is not available on this PC (common on laptops). Try Settings › System › Power.
pw.note: Ultimate is meant for desktops; on a laptop on battery prefer Balanced.
set.flicker.d: The "Welcome" sign on the Home page flickers like a real, half-broken neon sign. Turn it off for a steady sign. It also stays still when Windows animations are turned off.
page.net.s: Which programs talk to the internet, whether they go through your VPN, and known malicious addresses.
net.intro: Press "Analyze connections" to see every program that is connected to the internet right now.
net.geo.opt: Show country and company of each connection (sends the list of IP addresses to ip-api.com)
net.lists: Updating lists of known malicious addresses...
net.summary: {0} connections to the internet · {1} programs · malicious IP list: {2} addresses
net.vpn.off: NO VPN · your real IP {0} ({1}) is visible
net.nostatus: The VPN check could not be done (no internet?).
net.f.threat: Connects to a KNOWN MALICIOUS IP: {0}
net.f.threat.torrent: Connects to {0} IP(s) from a list of compromised computers ({1}). Common with torrents (other users), but stop any torrent you do not trust.
net.f.torrentleak: The TORRENT has {0} connection(s) OUTSIDE the VPN: your real IP is visible!
net.f.outside: {0} connection(s) outside the VPN (split tunneling or a leak)
net.f.unsigned: No digital signature (common for small harmless programs too)
net.f.temp: Runs from a Temp or Downloads folder: unusual for a normal program
net.f.remote: REMOTE ACCESS program: if you are not using it right now, close it (common in scams)
net.f.port: Port {0}: often used for remote control or by malware
net.vt.note: VirusTotal opens a search by the file's fingerprint (SHA256). Your file is never uploaded. "Trusted" hides minor warnings, but never malicious IPs or a torrent outside the VPN.
net.scan.clean: Microsoft Defender found no threats in {0}.
net.scan.found: Microsoft Defender found a THREAT in {0}! Open Windows Security to see what to do.
net.kill.confirm: End {0} now? Anything not saved in it will be lost.
net.kill.ms: ⚠ This is a Microsoft/Windows program. Ending it may cause problems.
net.listen.d: svchost, lsass, wininit, services, spoolsv and System belong to Windows. One port for the torrent program is normal. The firewall filters them.
net.mon.d: Shows every new connection the moment it opens. Beeps if something turns red (e.g. a torrent outside the VPN).
net.mon.started: Monitoring started ({0} existing connections are ignored)
net.rep.title: Network report
net.rep.note: These are indications, not certainty. For a definite answer, scan with your antivirus.
lo.intro: Finds broken entries left behind by programs you removed: startup items without a file, broken shortcuts, "ghost" installed apps and orphaned scheduled tasks. Nothing is removed without your tick, and a backup is always kept.
lo.none: ✓ No broken entries found. All clean!
lo.confirm: Remove {0} entries? A backup is kept and you can restore them.
lo.why.startup: Points to a program that no longer exists. Windows looks for it at every startup for nothing.
lo.why.shortcut: A shortcut to a program or file that no longer exists.
lo.why.uninstall: Listed under Installed apps, but the program is already gone and cannot be uninstalled.
lo.why.task: A task of a removed program that Windows keeps trying to run.
bf.intro: Finds the 40 largest files, so you can see what takes up space. Nothing is deleted automatically; you can send a file to the Recycle Bin.
hl.disk.bad: {0}: PROBLEM, back up your files now!
hl.uptime: Running for {0} days, {1} hours since the last restart
hl.uptime.long: {0} days without a restart. A restart helps Windows run smoothly.
hl.battery: Laptop battery: a detailed report shows how much capacity is left
hl.restart.confirm: Restart the PC now? Save your work first.
